### Mitochondrial transport

We study how mitochondrial membrane proteins recognize and transport metabolites and ions, how transport can be coupled to proton gradients, and how mutations or ligands reshape the underlying conformational landscape.

**Selected Publications:**

- “A novel model for proton transport mediated by uncoupling protein 1.” Jacobsen, L., Menon, S., Gaudry, M. J., Hakami Zanjani, A. A., Reinholdt, P., Jastroch, M. & Khandelia, H. ***Protein Sci*** **34**, e70357 (2025).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1002/pro.70357](https://doi.org/10.1002/pro.70357)

- “ATP-Bound State of the Uncoupling Protein 1 (UCP1) from Molecular Simulations.” Jacobsen, L., Lydersen, L. & Khandelia, H. ***J Phys Chem B*** **127**, 9685–9696 (2023).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcb.3c03473](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcb.3c03473)


### Psychedelic ligands and GPCRs

We investigate the molecular basis by which psychoactive ligands interact with G-protein-coupled receptors, with an emphasis on receptor conformational dynamics and experimentally testable molecular mechanisms. In particular, we have worked with the magic mushroom extract psilocin.

### Membrane proteins and ion transport

Transmembrane pumps and transporters use chemical or electrochemical energy to move ions and metabolites across membranes. We use MD simulations to investigate ion selectivity, transport pathways, coupling mechanisms and disease-causing perturbations. Systems studied in the group include the Na+,K+-ATPase, gastric H+,K+-ATPase, SERCA, KdpFABC and mitochondrial transport proteins.

### Nanoplastics

We investigate the structure of nanoplastic particles, their interactions with membranes and proteins, and computational strategies for their detection or removal from water.

**Selected Publications:**

- “Polymer Polydispersity and Lipid Composition Control Nanoplastic Disassembly in Membranes.” Ghermezcheshme, H., Bisht, K., Yesylevskyy, S. & Khandelia, H. ***bioRxiv*** (2026).

### Annexin-mediated membrane remodelling and repair

Cancer-cell plasma membranes experience substantial rupture stress. Annexins are Ca²⁺-sensitive phospholipid-binding proteins involved in membrane repair. Using all-atom and coarse-grained MD, the group has investigated how annexins bind, aggregate and induce curvature in damaged membranes, and how these mechanisms might be perturbed therapeutically.

**Selected Publications:**

- “Engineering a membrane-binding protein to trimerize and induce high membrane curvature.” Hakami Zanjani, A. A., Mularski, A., Heitmann, A. S. B., Dias, C., Møller, M. E., Maeda, K., Nylandsted, J., Simonsen, A. C. & Khandelia, H. ***Biophys J*** **122**, 3008–3017 (2023).

- “Interplay of membrane crosslinking and curvature induction by annexins.” Mularski, A., Sønder, S. L., Heitmann, A. S. B., Pandey, M. P., Khandelia, H., Nylandsted, J. & Simonsen, A. C. ***Sci Rep*** **12**, 22568 (2022).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-26633-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-26633-w)

- “Bending of a lipid membrane edge by annexin A5 trimers.” Pandey, M. P., Telles de Souza, P. C., Pezeshkian, W. & Khandelia, H. ***Biophys J*** **123**, 1006–1014 (2024).

### Membrane electromechanics

Lipid headgroups contain electrical dipoles. Curvature changes dipole density between the two leaflets of a bilayer and can therefore generate electrical polarization; conversely, transmembrane electric fields can influence membrane shape. We use simulation and theory to quantify this coupling between electrical potential and membrane mechanics.

**Selected Publications:**

- “Sensing membrane voltage by reorientation of dipolar transmembrane peptides.” Bisht, K., Lomholt, M. A. & Khandelia, H. ***Biophys J*** **123**, 584–597 (2024).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bpj.2024.01.037](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bpj.2024.01.037)

- “Thermodynamic Investigation of the Mechanism of Heat Production During Membrane Depolarization.” Bozorg, B., Lomholt, M. A. & Khandelia, H. ***J Phys Chem B*** **124**, 2815–2822 (2020).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcb.9b11456](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcb.9b11456)

- “Quantifying the Relationship between Curvature and Electric Potential in Lipid Bilayers.” Bruhn, D. S., Lomholt, M. A. & Khandelia, H. ***J Phys Chem B*** **120**, 4812–4817 (2016).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcb.6b03439](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcb.6b03439)


### Faster and enhanced molecular simulations

The group has developed virtual-site approaches that suppress fast hydrogen degrees of freedom in lipid simulations while retaining their non-bonded interactions, enabling longer integration time steps with all-atom membrane force fields. We also use enhanced-sampling and machine-learning approaches to extract mechanisms from complex molecular landscapes.

**Selected Publications:**

- “Accelerating All-Atom MD Simulations of Lipids Using a Modified Virtual-Sites Technique.” Loubet, B., Kopec, W. & Khandelia, H. ***J Chem Theory Comput*** **10**, 5690–5695 (2014).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1021/ct500100f](https://doi.org/10.1021/ct500100f)

- “Faster Simulations with a 5 fs Time Step for Lipids in the CHARMM Force Field.” Olesen, K., Awasthi, N., Bruhn, D. S., Pezeshkian, W. & Khandelia, H. ***J Chem Theory Comput*** **14**, 3342–3350 (2018).  
  [https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.8b00267](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.8b00267)

[Force-field files for the 5-fs lipid protocol](https://zenodo.org/record/1240161#.X3MQUpMzbVo)


### Drug–membrane and ligand–protein interactions

Small molecules can act not only through direct protein binding but also by changing membrane structure and dynamics. The group has investigated interactions of drugs and natural products with lipid bilayers, as well as ligand-induced changes in membrane proteins and receptors.


### Oxidized phospholipids

Oxidized phospholipids can strongly modify membrane chemistry, hydration and dynamics and are implicated in disease-associated cellular processes. Our simulations have examined their conformations, reorientation and interactions with cholesterol and other membrane components.
